At the root the tilted-square variance equals \(2as^2\), giving the exact negative normalized fourth derivative. Uniform Laplace estimates against the exact \(-2e^{-\lambda}\) curvature at \(a=1\) produce the \(3/2\log L\) and additive constant. The opposite small-shape beta expansion yields the error-function slope. The actual standalone diagnostic file passes 67 assertions; the proof, not finite checks, establishes the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The natural stationary peak-count boundary directly measures when a noisy harmonically trapped self-propelled particle stops accumulating away from the trap center. Its near-threshold leading inverse-logarithmic law hides a logarithmic-logarithmic displacement and a nonzero constant: these materially change finite-distance critical-noise predictions, while the opposite-limit explicit slope quantifies the first persistence-induced loss of the two-peak phase. Strict monotonicity and exact quartic degeneracy distinguish a genuine phase boundary from a numerical crossover; no paper-sized contribution is asserted.
